transcript:
Header: 2026-06-07 16:00 UTC | Duration: ~45m | Attendees: Alex Kim, Sanjay Patel, Leah Ortiz (Redwood); Rachel Gomez, Daniel Li, Maya Ortiz, Owen Park (EmberCloud)

Summary: quick renewal check, talk about expansion to EU region, capacity/dedicated pool sizing and contract extension options. Customer wants predictable p95 latency and cost control.

[00:00] Alex (Redwood): Hey everyone, thanks for joining, um we wanted to run through renewal timing and the expansion asks — add an EU region and maybe a dedicated pool, confirm SSO and SOC2 stuff. Quick intros?
[00:08] Rachel (EmberCloud): Hi Alex, Rachel here. Happy to be on, Daniel and Maya also are at the tail end of our contract and want to lock in quants for next year.
[00:15] Daniel (EmberCloud): Yeah we're evaluating whether to stay on hosted or move to dedicated for predictability — cost is a factor but latency spikes are biting during peak hours.
[00:25] Alex: Got it. Sanjay from our side will cover throughput/benchmarking and Leah will handle the compliance docs.
[00:30] Sanjay (Redwood SE): Hey all, quick note on dedicated: it buys you predictable GPU capacity and isolation. With our dedicated pools you can pin model ver, autoscale rules, and have guaranteed token throughput. The trade is price per token goes up a bit but p95 latency drops and variance is lower.
[00:48] Owen (EmberCloud): Can you quantify "a bit" — we're looking at a 30-40% cost delta?
[00:55] Alex: Typically you'd see 15-35% depending on batching, KV caching, and quantization profiles. If you commit longer term (2yr) we can push deeper discounts and include multi-region capacity discounts as well.
[01:12] Maya (EmberCloud): For EU region, data residency is a hard requirement for some of our customers. Need to know latency targets — p95 under 300ms is our goal.
[01:22] Sanjay: p95 <300ms is doable; depends on model size, seq length, and whether you use cross-region fallbacks. For EU we recommend running an EU-dedicated pool colocated in eu-west-1 (or eu-central) and enabling prefix caching for common prompts, that drops effective token compute. We'll show numbers in the benchmark.
[01:40] Rachel: Also security: we need SOC2, SAML SSO, and KMS integration. Any blockers?
[01:47] Leah (Redwood CSM): We have SOC2 docs and a KMS/HSM integration pattern; SAML SSO + SCIM for provisioning is supported. We'll drop the trust pack into the shared link after the call.
[01:58] Daniel: Are audit logs available at token-level, or just request-level? We need detailed traces for compliance.
[02:06] Leah: We provide per-request tracing, token-level cost breakdown in Console, and full audit logs for enterprise/private customers. For private deployments we can integrate with customer logging endpoints.
[02:15] Rachel: On performance — we ran a small pilot last quarter on hosted and saw p95 spiky at around 450ms during afternoon peaks. We want to baseline what dedicated would give us.
[02:26] Sanjay: Perfect. For the benchmark plan I propose: 1) replicate sample traffic shape (qps/time-of-day) 2) run 30m steady-state and 30m burst test 3) measure p50/p95/p99 and request fallbacks. We'll test with and without KV cache and with recommended quantization profile.
[02:45] Daniel: How about private VPC? We're sensitive about data leaving our VPC — private control plane option?
[02:52] Alex: Yes we offer Private (VPC) deployments with customer-managed networking or on-prem options; there's an enterprise package for that. It's heavier lift but meets strict regs. That said, many customers go with dedicated hosted pools in the same cloud region and get the compliance they need combined with RBC and encryption in transit and at rest.
[03:10] Owen: Does private mean we manage keys or Redwood can manage?
[03:13] Leah: You can do either: customer-managed KMS is supported (bring-your-own-key), or Redwood-managed KMS for convenience.
[03:19] Rachel: Contract term — what incentives if we extend to 2 years and commit to X shards?
[03:25] Alex: We can offer stepped discounts: standard 1yr pricing, and deeper discount for 2yr and committed capacity. Also, multi-region bundles (e.g., US + EU) get an incremental discount. I'll put options in the quote.
[03:36] Maya: Operationally, we'd like to start with a canary rollout in EU region and then shift traffic. Any recommended rollout approach?
[03:42] Sanjay: Canary + traffic ramp with A/B routing by user segment is the usual. Redwood supports canary rollouts and automatic fallback to the baseline model or to hosted region if the EU pool is overloaded.
[03:53] Daniel: Any latency cost for fallback?
[03:55] Sanjay: There's cross-region added latency if you fallback to a US region; we can gate that with policy and show the expected p95 in the benchmark.
[04:03] Rachel: Okay good. On the audit side, we'd need the compliance contact to sign a data processing addendum — can you send that?
[04:09] Leah: Yes will send DPA and the SOC2 package.
[04:12] Alex: Next steps recap — I'll send revised quote with term options and multi-region sizing; Sanjay will share a benchmark plan and proposed dates; Leah to share SOC2/KMS/SSO docs; Rachel to share traffic profile and compliance contact.
[04:25] Rachel: Sounds good. One quick Q — competitors: we're also evaluating Anthropic and some in-house options; main tie-breakers are predictable cost and operational simplicity.
[04:33] Alex: Understood. We'll make the quote and benchmark results speak to that — show economics and p95 improvement for dedicated.
[04:38] Daniel: Timeline — we're aiming to finalize by end of month and onboard EU region in Q3 if all good.
[04:44] Alex: Great. We'll try to accelerate the pricing and get the SE deep-dive scheduled next week.
[04:48] Rachel: Thanks everyone.
[04:50] Alex: Thanks — action items summarized and will follow up in email.

End of call.
